title: Developmental Writability and Synaptic Selection in Schizophrenia: Prepared Priors, Gated Encoding, and Recursive Fixation
content: Background and Hypothesis: Schizophrenia poses a developmental problem and a content problem: sustained psychosis commonly emerges during late neurodevelopment, while delusions are diverse yet repeatedly organized around threat, agency, self-reference, status, control, and related human concerns. We hypothesize that these features can be linked by biased developmental writing within a structured representational landscape. Study Design: This Major Review integrates clinical phenomenology, delusional-theme meta-analysis, human developmental neurobiology, synaptic and molecular schizophrenia findings, computational learning studies, and causal evidence from sensitive-period learning. ARCH × Φ is reformulated as a two-layer execution-encoding architecture in which a transient permissive state continuously gates the rate at which selected activity modifies a persistent substrate. Study Results: The synthesis yields five separations: acute inference is not durable encoding; salience is not target selection; prepared priors constrain candidate content without fixing specific delusions; stabilization and elimination can dissociate; and persistence resides in modified substrate rather than in the transient gate. A labile-to-persistent two-candidate model separates modification drive from writability, exhibits a critical writability regime for fixation, and becomes probabilistic near that boundary when stochastic variation is introduced. Conclusions: The framework recasts adolescent synaptic pathology as abnormal developmental selection rather than pruning alone. It predicts that strong anomalous experiences need not consolidate below a critical writability regime, whereas above that regime small content biases can become persistent. Longitudinal tests must measure acute drive and durable writing separately. Explicit observations that would disconfirm prepared-prior, gating, synaptic-selection, and recursive claims are specified.
